B_license.evidence_source: The pinned repository README.md itself explicitly declares Apache-2.0 in BOTH the YAML frontmatter metadata field (license: apache-2.0, line 13) AND in first-party prose text within the README body (line 29: '- Released under the **Apache 2 License**') -- no standalone LICENSE/LICENSE.md/LICENSE.txt file exists in the repository (all three checked, all HTTP 404 at the pinned revision).
B_license.note: Phase 21B.4.16.1 correction: the prior phase's wording ('README.md YAML frontmatter tag only') understated the actual first-party evidence. The persisted README contains an explicit PROSE statement -- '- Released under the **Apache 2 License**' (line 29) -- in addition to the structured cardData.license metadata tag (line 13); these are two independent first-party declarations of the same license, not one metadata tag alone. Apache-2.0 identification is therefore directly supported by the repository's own first-party content (metadata AND prose), not merely inferred from a tag. The absence of a standalone full-license-text file remains an accurate evidentiary-FORMAT fact (this repository does not host a local copy of the canonical Apache-2.0 legal text) but is not, and was never, a license-identity AMBIGUITY. The repository's 'extra_gated_description' is informational only (a Privacy Policy link) and the API's own 'gated' field confirms false -- no genuine access restriction exists.

D_tokenizer_identity.note: Tokenizer identity pinned at the same repository revision. Repository carries a 'mistral-common' tag AND ships a full HF-transformers-compatible tokenizer_config.json with a populated chat_template -- both paths coexist (see H_chat_template below, closed in Phase 21B.4.16.1).

F_weight_layout.actual_repository_weight_layout: DUAL FORMAT -- both a single-file 'consolidated.safetensors' (24,495,604,224 bytes) AND a standard 5-shard HF set (model-00001..00005-of-00005.safetensors) storing the SAME BF16 weights redundantly. Real per-format size is ~22.8 GiB; the API's usedStorage figure (49.04 GB) reflects both formats combined, not double the actual model size.
F_weight_layout.note: Matches the registry's existing bf16_gb=24.5 figure closely, confirmed via live blobs=true metadata this phase (not merely re-stated).

G_context_window.note: 131072 (128K) native context, confirmed directly from config.json at the pinned revision -- substantially larger than both other controls.

H_chat_template.dual_path_confirmed: The repository ships BOTH a standard HF-transformers-compatible tokenizer_config.json with a populated chat_template jinja field (usable directly by vLLM's OpenAI-compatible server) AND the Mistral-native tooling path (params.json + consolidated.safetensors + tekken.json, the mistral-common/mistral-inference-native representation).
H_chat_template.note: Phase 21B.4.16.1 correction: the prior phase inferred the chat-formatting path solely from the 'mistral-common' repository tag without inspecting tokenizer_config.json. Direct inspection this phase found tokenizer_config.json DOES exist and DOES contain a populated chat_template -- the prior 'likely runs through mistral-common rather than a plain chat_template.jinja' framing was too weak; both paths coexist.

I_reasoning_thinking_mode.note: Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 is a standard instruct model, not part of a hybrid-thinking family -- no reasoning/thinking-mode parser requirement expected.

vllm.note: No dedicated recipe page exists, but the repository's own HF metadata declares library_name='vllm' -- a structural signal that vLLM is the officially expected/canonical serving path for this repository, even without a dedicated recipe write-up.

transformers.note: MistralForCausalLM confirmed as a supported architecture in vLLM's own official supported-models documentation (docs/orneur/phase-21/evidence/GENESIS_CONTROL_SET_VLLM_SUPPORTED_MODELS_PRIMARY_SOURCE_2026-09-23.md) -- the Example HF Models column lists other Mistral models (Ministral-3, Mistral-7B family), not Mistral-Nemo-Instruct-2407 by name, so this is architecture-class support evidence, not model-specific confirmation; recorded honestly as that weaker evidence tier.

K_likely_future_topology.raw_weight_fit_note: 24,495,604,224 bytes (~24.50 GB decimal / ~22.81 GiB) BF16 weight footprint EXCEEDS a 24GB-class GPU's raw usable capacity by weight size alone -- a GPU marketed as 24 GB does not provide >24,495,604,224 bytes of usable model memory, and runtime/KV allocations require additional space beyond the raw weight floor regardless. The prior phase's framing ('BORDERLINE ... little to no headroom') incorrectly implied a possible fit; corrected here to a clear NO.
K_likely_future_topology.production_serving_qualification_note: No topology is claimed as qualified regardless of raw fit.

minimum_plausible_native_precision_topol.statement: A single 24GB-class GPU does NOT raw-fit the ~24.5 GB BF16 weight set. A native-BF16 topology requires either a larger single card (e.g. an 80GB+-class GPU) or a multi-GPU topology explicitly supported by the chosen runtime -- no exact topology is claimed as qualified.

safer_qualification_topology.statement: 1x H100/H200-class GPU (80GB+) is the safer minimum for a bounded BF16 production-serving smoke, since it raw-fits the weight set with real headroom and avoids relying on unconfirmed multi-GPU tensor-parallel behavior for this architecture/runtime combination.

quantized_topology_options.statement: FP8 (~12.2 GB) and INT4 (~6.1 GB) both raw-fit a single 24GB-class GPU by weight size alone; no official quantized artifact confirmed this phase.

L_precision_options.native_precision_artifact: BF16 (this repository, in dual on-disk format)
L_precision_options.note: Per phase instruction: a quantized derivative, if used in a future execution, must not be treated as the same registered control identity unless the locked evaluation protocol explicitly authorizes that precision/artifact -- this control's registered identity is the BF16 repository above.

M_special_requirements.mistral_common_package: Relevant per the repository's own 'mistral-common' tag -- a future runtime harness should verify whether mistral-common is required for correct chat-template/tokenizer behavior, or whether the standard transformers/vLLM path suffices.

N_zero_owner_cash_classification.rationale: No GPU execution was performed to determine this. The BF16 weight footprint is borderline on a 24GB-class GPU and safer on an 80GB+-class GPU; a future zero-cash smoke is plausible but not confirmed AVAILABLE_NOW absent a live credit-availability check. No promotional credits, account balance, or prior-phase credit state is assumed.

O_engine_decision.rationale: The repository's own library_name='vllm' metadata tag is a direct, structural signal of the officially expected serving path, even absent a dedicated recipe page. ORNEUR's existing validated vLLM harness experience is a real implementation-risk advantage. SGLang not selected as fallback due to no confirmed official support evidence for this control this phase.
